World Bank Group - Umbrella Facility for Trade 2.0

description.narrative: The World Banks´s “Umbrella Facility for Trade Multi Donor Trust Fund (UFT) 2.0, including the Trade Facilitation Support Program (TFSP) which was integrated as a part of UFT, is the World Bank’s channel for supporting WB's trade-related development assistance. The development objective is to foster trade in low- and middle-income countries that is green, resilient and inclusive.. The UFT 2.0 will enhance social and environmental impacts of trade through knowledge products, capacity building and through leveraging WBG trade related lending.

Världsbankens "Umbrella Facility for Trade Multi Donor Trust Fund (UFT) 2.0", inklusive Trade Facilitation Support Program (TFSP) som integrerades som en del av UFT, är Världsbankens kanal för deras handelsrelaterade utvecklingsbistånd. Utvecklingsmålet är att främja grön, motståndskraftig och inkluderande handel i låg- och medelinkomstländer. UFT 2.0 kommer att förstärka sociala och miljömässiga effekter av handel genom kunskapsprodukter, kapacitetsuppbyggnad och genom att katalysera och skala-upp VB:s handelsrelaterade utlåning.

The development objective of UFT 2.0 is to contribute to fostering trade in low- and middle-income countries that is green, resilient and inclusive which contributes to economic growth and poverty reduction.
The work is based on three thematic Pillars:
Pillar 1: Improving countries market access and deepening trade relationships
Pillar 2: Boosting firms competitiveness and particpation in GVCs
Pillar 3: Facilitating trade and strengthening its resilience
Three outputs that will contribute to reach outcomes and the objective are:
1. Institutional knowledge and capacity to assess the implications and distributional impacts of evolving trade accession, openness and integration opportunities.
2. Institutional and regulatory framework, knowledge capacity and infrastructure to support firm trade competitiveness and value chain integration.
3. Technical assistance and capacity to implement and monitor border management and trade facilitation agreements in goods and services.
In addition priority trade issues will be revisited every two years and for the first two years will focus on:
i) the trade ecosystem resilience and diversification; ii) climate, environmental sustainability and social inclusivity; and iii) data and innovation-driven services.
